option_relations.rationale: Right ventricular infarction is a component of the more specific diagnosis described in the leaf, which includes the cause (proximal RCA occlusion) and other affected areas (inferior wall).

The option describes mirror-image dextrocardia in addition to the myocardial infarction described in the leaf. While the leaf focuses on the MI, the option provides a broader, more complete diagnosis that includes the MI and its cause.

Acute inferior-lateral ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is a broader category that encompasses the specific myocardial infarction described in the leaf, which is due to proximal right coronary artery occlusion and affects the inferior wall.

The option 'Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction due to proximal right coronary artery occlusion' is clinically equivalent to the leaf 'Acute myocardial infarction due to total occlusion of the proximal right coronary artery', as 'total occlusion' implies 'ST-elevation' in this context and both describe the same event and etiology.
